walkthroughs.body_html:
Power: Monarchy & Democracy in Britain c1000 to 2014 — a core area of GCSE History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Power: Monarchy & Democracy in Britain c1000 to 2014 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Power: Monarchy & Democracy in Britain c1000 to 2014.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: William Marshal
Simon de Montfort
Thomas Becket
John Wycliffe

options: London
Manchester
Birmingham
Liverpool

mcqs.q: What did the 1832 Great Reform Act actually do?
options: It abolished rotten boroughs, redistributed seats to industrial towns, and extended the vote to about 1 in 5 adult men — still far short of democracy.
The 1832 Reform Act allowed women to vote for the first time.
The 1832 Reform Act gave the vote to all working men.
Because Britain banned slavery before other countries.

mcqs.q: Why did the Industrial Revolution begin in Britain?
options: Because James Watt invented the steam engine.
The 1832 Reform Act allowed women to vote for the first time.
A combination of capital from trade and empire, coal and iron deposits, agricultural improvements, political stability, and a culture of invention.
Because Britain banned slavery before other countries.
